{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./somd_array_gpu.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -n 1             -> -n 1
#   --gres=gpu:1     -> -g 1
#   --time 24:00:00  -> -t 24h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 24h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p main not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the main partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o somd-array-gpu-%A.%a.out uses %A/%a expansions (jobid/array index) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you generate unique filenames.

  echo "CUDA DEVICES:" "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"

  mkdir -p 10cycles
  cd 10cycles || exit 1

  export OPENMM_PLUGIN_DIR=/home/julien/sire.app/lib/plugins/

  flux run -n 1 -g 1 ~/sire.app/bin/somd-freenrg -C ../sim10.cfg -l 0.50 -p CUDA

  cd ..
fi
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
